extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU (Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning) is a benchmark of 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering) across 30 subjects and 183 subfields. It features 30 heterogeneous image types and is designed to evaluate expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning in large multimodal models.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were manually collected by a team of over 50 college students (including co-authors) specializing in various majors. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, and created new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and to select questions without immediately available answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials across 30 subjects and 6 disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in relevant majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, and to create new questions based on their expertise. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoid data from sites prohibiting copying or redistribution, and select questions without immediately available answers. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence. Authors also categorized problems into difficulty levels and excluded approximately 10% classified as very easy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. A second stage involved distributing problems among co-authors for format and typo checking. A third stage had authors categorize problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), with approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students specializing in the relevant majors (college students from various disciplines)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle; the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI; a few subjects like law and linguistics were excluded because it is difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems in these subjects
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Expert AGI marks a critical milestone denoting an AI system that reaches 'at least 90th percentile of skilled adults' in a broad range of tasks, starting to achieve 'the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor' for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption; the authors believe MMMU will stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning; benchmarking expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models; monitoring progress towards Expert AGI; developing next-generation multimodal foundation models
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, followed by author review to eliminate duplications. Format and typo checking by co-authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format. Exclusion of approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy (very easy difficulty level) that did not align with the design criteria.
